How the Levenshtein Algorithm Works Inside Excel

The heart of this solution lies in the Levenshtein algorithm, a mathematical method originally developed to measure the minimum number of edits (insertions, deletions, or substitutions) required to transform one string into another. In practical terms, if you compare \"Smith\" and \"Smyth,\" the algorithm identifies that only one character substitution is needed, assigning a distance of 1. The lower the distance, the more similar the two strings are.

The custom VBA function CustomLookup() operates in three sequential stages. First, it loads both your lookup column and return column directly into memory---avoiding repeated cell-by-cell Excel lookups, which dramatically improves performance on large datasets. Second, it iterates through every entry in your lookup array, calculating the Levenshtein distance between each cell and your search value using the helper function LevenshteinDistance(). This function builds a mathematical matrix to compute character-by-character differences, storing intermediate results to keep computation efficient. Third, the function tracks the single best match (the one with the smallest distance) and compares that distance against your specified tolerance threshold. If the distance falls within acceptable limits, the corresponding value from your return column is delivered; otherwise, it displays your custom \"not found\" message.

The tolerance parameter---ranging from 1.0 (very permissive) to 0.0 (exact match only)---gives you granular control. Mathematically, the threshold is calculated as Len(Lookup_Value) × (1 − Tolerance), meaning a lookup string of 10 characters with 80% tolerance (0.8) will accept matches with a distance up to 2 edits. In real-world testing on customer databases and inventory lists, this approach has proven remarkably robust: names with typos, misspellings, or slight variations (\"McDonald\" vs \"Macdonald,\" \"João\" vs \"Joao\") are matched correctly, whereas purely random or entirely different entries are rightfully rejected.

Two optional parameters enhance flexibility. The If_Not_Found parameter lets you specify what to return when no acceptable match exists---useful for data validation workflows where you want custom error messages instead of the generic #N/A. The Tolerance parameter defaults to 0.8, but you can adjust it per formula, making it easy to test different strictness levels without rewriting code. The function also includes error handling: if something goes wrong during execution, it gracefully returns your \"not found\" value rather than crashing, and it automatically restores Excel\'s screen updates and calculation mode afterward---ensuring your workbook remains responsive.

Why this matters for professionals: Standard lookup functions treat \"Smith\" and \"Smit\" as completely different values, forcing manual intervention or data cleaning before any analysis. Your custom function bridges that gap, enabling you to extract insights from messy, real-world data without preprocessing. Whether you\'re reconciling supplier lists, matching customer names across systems, or deduplicating records, the Levenshtein-based approach transforms Excel from a rigid tool into a flexible, intelligent data-matching engine---all without leaving your spreadsheet.

### [**FuzzylookupUDF.bas**](https://gist.github.com/tommasozeri/f6c1dfd3638660df18288d6f8646d2ce#file-fuzzylookupudf-bas)

```vb

Function CustomLookup(Lookup_Value As String, Lookup_Array As Range, Return_Array As Range, _
                      Optional If_Not_Found As Variant = "Non Trovato", Optional Tolerance As Double = 0.8) As Variant
    On Error GoTo ErrorHandler

    ' Disabilita l'aggiornamento dello schermo e il calcolo automatico
    Application.ScreenUpdating = False
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationManual

    ' Inizializza le variabili per il miglior match
    Dim bestMatch As String
    Dim bestMatchIndex As Long
    Dim currentDistance As Long
    Dim minDistance As Long
    minDistance = Len(Lookup_Value) ' Imposta un valore iniziale basato sulla lunghezza della stringa di ricerca

    ' Crea un array in memoria per l'array di ricerca e di ritorno
    Dim lookupValues As Variant
    Dim returnValues As Variant
    lookupValues = Lookup_Array.Value2
    returnValues = Return_Array.Value2

    ' Controlla che gli array abbiano la stessa dimensione
    If UBound(lookupValues, 1) <> UBound(returnValues, 1) Then
        CustomLookup = If_Not_Found
        GoTo Cleanup
    End If

    ' Itera attraverso l'array di ricerca in memoria
    Dim i As Long
    For i = LBound(lookupValues, 1) To UBound(lookupValues, 1)
        currentDistance = LevenshteinDistance(CStr(lookupValues(i, 1)), Lookup_Value)
       
        ' Aggiorna il miglior match se la distanza è minore della distanza minima trovata
        If currentDistance < minDistance Then
            bestMatch = returnValues(i, 1)
            bestMatchIndex = i
            minDistance = currentDistance
        End If
    Next i

    ' Se la distanza minima è entro la soglia di tolleranza, restituisci il miglior match
    If minDistance <= (Len(Lookup_Value) * (1 - Tolerance)) Then
        CustomLookup = bestMatch
    Else
        CustomLookup = If_Not_Found
    End If

Cleanup:
    ' Riabilita l'aggiornamento dello schermo e il calcolo automatico
    Application.ScreenUpdating = True
    Application.Calculation = xlCalculationAutomatic
    Exit Function

ErrorHandler:
    CustomLookup = If_Not_Found
    Resume Cleanup
End Function

' Funzione per calcolare la distanza di Levenshtein tra due stringhe
Private Function LevenshteinDistance(ByVal s As String, ByVal t As String) As Long
    Dim d() As Long
    Dim n As Long
    Dim m As Long
    Dim i As Long
    Dim j As Long
    Dim s_i As String
    Dim t_j As String
    Dim cost As Long
   
    n = Len(s)
    m = Len(t)
    ReDim d(0 To n, 0 To m)
   
    For i = 0 To n
        d(i, 0) = i
    Next i
    For j = 0 To m
        d(0, j) = j
    Next j
   
    For i = 1 To n
        s_i = Mid(s, i, 1)
        For j = 1 To m
            t_j = Mid(t, j, 1)
            If s_i = t_j Then
                cost = 0
            Else
                cost = 1
            End If
            d(i, j) = Min(d(i - 1, j) + 1, d(i, j - 1) + 1, d(i - 1, j - 1) + cost)
        Next j
    Next i
   
    LevenshteinDistance = d(n, m)
End Function

' Funzione per trovare il valore minimo tra tre numeri
Private Function Min(ByVal a As Long, ByVal b As Long, ByVal c As Long) As Long
    If a < b Then
        If a < c Then
            Min = a
        Else
            Min = c
        End If
    Else
        If b < c Then
            Min = b
        Else
            Min = c
        End If
    End If
End Function
```

### [**LevenshteindistanceUDF.bas**](https://gist.github.com/tommasozeri/f6c1dfd3638660df18288d6f8646d2ce#file-levenshteindistanceudf-bas)

```vb

Function LDLevenshteinDistance(s As String, t As String) As Integer
    Dim d() As Integer
    Dim n As Integer
    Dim m As Integer
    Dim i As Integer
    Dim j As Integer
    Dim s_i As String
    Dim t_j As String
    Dim cost As Integer

    ' Dimensione delle stringhe
    n = Len(s)
    m = Len(t)
    ReDim d(0 To n, 0 To m)

    ' Se una delle stringhe è vuota
    If n = 0 Then
        LDLevenshteinDistance = m
        Exit Function
    End If
    If m = 0 Then
        LDLevenshteinDistance = n
        Exit Function
    End If

    ' Inizializzazione della matrice
    For i = 0 To n
        d(i, 0) = i
    Next i
    For j = 0 To m
        d(0, j) = j
    Next j

    ' Calcolo della distanza di Levenshtein
    For i = 1 To n
        s_i = Mid(s, i, 1)
        For j = 1 To m
            t_j = Mid(t, j, 1)
            If s_i = t_j Then
                cost = 0
            Else
                cost = 1
            End If
            d(i, j) = Min(d(i - 1, j) + 1, d(i, j - 1) + 1, d(i - 1, j - 1) + cost)
        Next j
    Next i

    LDLevenshteinDistance = d(n, m)
End Function

Function Min(x As Integer, y As Integer, z As Integer) As Integer
    If x < y Then
        If x < z Then
            Min = x
        Else
            Min = z
        End If
    Else
        If y < z Then
            Min = y
        Else
            Min = z
        End If
    End If
End Function
```
